base_instruction: You are a helpful meal planning assistant. Help the user plan a baby shower brunch menu by tracking who is attending, their dietary needs, and any logistics. When the user asks you to evaluate specific menu items, check each item against every active guest's current dietary constraints. Pay close attention to changes in the guest list and any updates throughout the conversation.

state_queue.anchor: Hey, I'm throwing a baby shower brunch for my friend Megan this Saturday and I need help planning the menu. Any ideas?

flow_info.value: Five guests confirmed: me, Megan (the mom-to-be), Priya, Noor, and Aunt Linda
Priya was diagnosed with celiac disease last year
Noor moved here from Jordan a couple years ago. She is a practicing Muslim
Aunt Linda has had type 2 diabetes for about ten years now
Budget is around 200 dollars total for food
Priya just texted me — she threw out her back this morning and can't make it. But she asked if I could save her a plate to drop off later
Aunt Linda told me her doctor just put her on a strict low-sodium diet on top of the diabetes management
Megan's cousin Rachel is coming too, so that's one more
Rachel had a really bad reaction to scrambled eggs at a diner last month — her face swelled up and they had to use an EpiPen
Menu items to check: smoked salmon bagels, spinach and feta quiche, fresh fruit salad with honey-lime dressing, bacon-wrapped dates, Belgian waffles with whipped cream, and a mimosa bar

constraints.value: Cannot eat raw or smoked fish, unpasteurized cheese, raw eggs, or consume alcohol
inference_chain: 7 months pregnant → pregnancy dietary restrictions apply
Pregnancy → no raw/smoked fish, no unpasteurized cheese, no alcohol, no raw eggs

constraints.surface_form: Priya was diagnosed with celiac disease last year

Gluten → must avoid wheat, barley, rye, and cross-contaminated products

constraints.value: Cannot eat pork or pork-derived products, cannot consume alcohol
constraints.surface_form: Noor moved here from Jordan a couple years ago. She is a practicing Muslim
inference_chain: Practicing Muslim → follows halal dietary laws
Halal → no pork or pork-derived products, no alcohol

constraints.value: Must limit sugar and refined carbohydrates
constraints.surface_form: Aunt Linda has had type 2 diabetes for about ten years now
inference_chain: Type 2 diabetes → must manage blood sugar
Blood sugar management → limit sugar and refined carbohydrates

constraints.value: Must follow a strict low-sodium diet
constraints.surface_form: Aunt Linda told me her doctor just put her on a strict low-sodium diet on top of the diabetes management

constraints.value: Cannot eat eggs or egg-containing products
constraints.surface_form: Rachel had a really bad reaction to scrambled eggs at a diner last month — her face swelled up and they had to use an EpiPen
inference_chain: Severe reaction to scrambled eggs + facial swelling + EpiPen → egg allergy

hidden_state.value: You are hosting a baby shower brunch for your pregnant friend Megan. You will introduce the guest list and their backgrounds across the first couple of turns, then share updates as people drop out or join. At the end, you will share a specific menu and ask if there are any issues. You never hint at what the problems might be — you just ask openly.

You are a calm, cheerful host planning a party. You always refer to your guests by name in third person (e.g. 'Priya texted me...', 'Aunt Linda told me...'). You never express frustration or impatience when plans change. You treat each update as normal party planning coordination.
hidden_state.description: Prevents emotion escalation and ensures third-person relay for guest updates

ground_truth.answer: Smoked salmon bagels: problematic for Megan (smoked fish is unsafe during pregnancy), and bagels contain gluten so this cannot go on Priya's saved plate. Spinach and feta quiche: problematic for Rachel (quiche contains eggs, she has an egg allergy), and contains gluten so cannot go on Priya's saved plate. Fresh fruit salad with honey-lime dressing: fine for everyone at the table and fine for Priya's saved plate. Bacon-wrapped dates: problematic for Noor (bacon is pork, she follows halal). Belgian waffles with whipped cream: problematic for Rachel (waffles contain eggs), high in sugar which is a concern for Aunt Linda (type 2 diabetes), and contain gluten so cannot go on Priya's saved plate. Mimosa bar: problematic for Megan (alcohol during pregnancy) and for Noor (alcohol is not halal).

ground_truth.explanation: This scenario tests entity lifecycle tracking and inferential constraint reasoning across a baby shower brunch planning conversation. The agent must track: (1) Megan is 7 months pregnant → pregnancy dietary restrictions → no smoked fish, no alcohol (inferential chain), (2) Priya has celiac disease → no gluten (inferential), (3) Noor is a practicing Muslim from Jordan → halal → no pork, no alcohol (inferential), (4) Aunt Linda has type 2 diabetes → limit sugar (inferential), then gets a constraint UPGRADE with strict low-sodium added, (5) Priya EXITS the brunch but needs a saved plate → her gluten constraint shifts from table scope to saved-plate scope, (6) Rachel JOINS late with an inferential constraint: severe reaction to scrambled eggs + EpiPen → egg allergy. At probe time, the agent must apply CURRENT constraint state: Megan = no smoked fish, no alcohol; Noor = no pork, no alcohol; Rachel = no eggs; Aunt Linda = low sugar + low sodium; Priya = not at table but saved plate must be gluten-free. The fruit salad is the clearly-fine item. Bacon-wrapped dates test the pork-halal inference. Smoked salmon bagels test pregnancy knowledge. Quiche and waffles test the late-joining Rachel's egg allergy. The mimosa bar tests both pregnancy and halal alcohol restrictions. The scope distinction is that Priya's gluten constraint only applies to the saved plate, not to what is served at the table.

mechanism: Entity EXIT with scope change: person leaves but wants something packed/saved
